areas.name: Principal Engineer Plan
areas.description: 52 weeks of deliberate practice: Senior Staff to top 1% Principal. Four quarters, each with an exit gate. Practice deliberately, measure honestly, don't stop.
areas.standard: People fear bringing bad work to me. They never fear me. They love me because I make their work better and give them credit for it.
areas.nextSteps: Read the standard every Monday. Name the one thing only you can do this week.

notes.title: The ten rules
notes.body:
1. Fear attaches to the work, never the person. Critique the design. Respect the engineer.
2. Publish your bar. People can only rise to a standard they can see.
3. Apply one standard to everyone.
4. Be precise, not harsh. Point to the line, the trace, the number.
5. Never soften a real blocker. Calm, specific and unmovable beats loud.
6. Praise in public, specifically.
7. Follow up on conditions.
8. Own your mistakes first and out loud.
9. Speak last in meetings. Summarise both sides better than they did, then decide.
10. Bring leaders decisions, not problems: two options, your recommendation, the risk of each.

Warning sign: if people stop showing you half-formed ideas, your fear has leaked from the work onto you. Add warmth. Keep the bar.

notes.title: Operating rhythm
notes.body:
Daily: 90-minute deep block, protected. Log every estimate and risk call before saying it. One specific piece of public praise.

Weekly: Monday, the one thing only you can do. 3-4 hours of lab work. 1 hour of mentoring. One public postmortem with the root cause predicted first. Friday, the weekly review.

Monthly: score the estimate log (what % landed inside the 90% range?). Score the risk log (Brier). Reread decision-journal entries from 1 and 3 months ago. Manager check-in.

Quarterly: pass the gate. Ask a peer, a junior and a leader: more of, less of? Score all seven goals 1-5. Ask: do people still bring me half-formed ideas? Rebalance time toward the lagging goal.

notes.title: Weekly time budget
notes.body:
Priority check - Monday morning, 20 min - name the one thing only you can do this week.
Deep block - every workday morning, 90 min x 5 - design, review, writing. No meetings, no chat.
Lab block - one evening or weekend morning, 3-4 h - build, break, measure.
Mentoring - fixed weekly slot, 1 h - required for G6.
Friday score - end of day, 10 min - the weekly review.

notes.title: Review checklist v1
notes.body:
Tier every item: B blocking, I important, N nit. Rewrite this in week 9 from your own misses.

Problem - Is this the right problem? What happens if we do nothing? Is there a simpler option?
Approach - Why this design over the two obvious alternatives? What does it cost at 10x scale?
Failure - Dependency slow, not down? Message duplicated or out of order? Partial deploy? Rollback path?
Data - Is every write idempotent? Where can two systems disagree? How do we reconcile?
Load - Where is the backpressure? What bounds the queue, the pool, the retry?
Observability - How do we know it broke before a customer does? Which alert, which dashboard?
Security - Who can call this? What leaks if logs, caches or prompts are exposed?
Cost - What does it cost per month at today's volume and at peak?
Operability - Who gets paged at 3 a.m.? Can they fix it without the author?

End every review with one line: Approve, Approve with conditions, or Rework, plus the single most important reason.

notes.title: Estimation and risk method
notes.body:
Estimation: reference class first - ask how long the last three similar pieces of work took, anchor there, then adjust. Always give two ranges: 50% likely, 90% you would be surprised to land outside. Separate effort from calendar; reviews, dependencies and integration often double calendar time. Score monthly: if fewer than 85% of actuals land inside your 90% range, widen your ranges.

Risk: pre-mortem - 'it is six months later and this failed, why?' Everyone writes silently for five minutes first. Rate each risk on likelihood, blast radius and detectability; undetectable risks get the most attention. State risk as a probability and a resolve-by date. Brier = (probability - outcome)^2, averaged. 0.25 is a coin flip; target under 0.20.

Both logs live in /log. Write the call down before you say it out loud.

notes.title: Turn the job into the training ground
notes.body:
Design reviews -> write four layers: right problem, right approach, production failure, details. End with a one-line verdict.
Giving estimates -> log the 50% and 90% range before you say the number out loud.
Project kickoffs -> run a 30-minute pre-mortem. Log the top risks with probabilities.
Incidents -> write your root-cause guess before reading the analysis. Score it.
Architecture decisions -> write a decision-journal entry. Name what would prove you wrong.
Meetings you chair -> speak last. Summarise both sides. Decide.

notes.title: Handling slippage
notes.body:
Never miss twice in a row. One missed week is noise; two is a new habit.
Shrink, don't skip. No time for a 90-minute kata? Do 20 minutes. Keep the chain alive.
Rebalance quarterly, not weekly. Move time to lagging goals at the quarter review. Don't redesign the plan every week.

tasks.title: Audit one week of calendar; mark every meeting where I add nothing unique
Decline or delegate at least half of those meetings
Block 90 minutes every weekday morning for the next 13 weeks
Block one 3-4 hour lab session every week
Tell my manager the three goals for the quarter; ask for a monthly check-in
Find one training partner to swap design katas with every two weeks

goals.title: G1 Understand distributed systems by breaking them
goals.outcome: 70%+ of failure predictions correct in the lab and at work.
goals.notes: Predict how a system fails before you test it, and be right most of the time. Log every prediction in /log as a call.

goals.title: G2 Be an elite reviewer
goals.outcome: Catch 70%+ of root causes in cold reviews of designs that later failed.
goals.notes: Find the flaw before production does. Teams answer your questions in the doc before you ask. Baseline in week 8; +15 points by the Q2 gate.
links: Q2 Elite reviewer and GenAI fluency

goals.title: G3 Estimate and assess risk accurately
goals.outcome: 90% ranges contain the actual 85%+ of the time. Brier under 0.20.
goals.notes: Give ranges, not guesses. Both figures are the ones /log computes; 0.25 is a coin flip.

goals.title: G4 Lead with GenAI, not just use it
goals.outcome: One agent and one eval harness built from scratch. One AI practice adopted by 2+ teams.
goals.notes: Build agents and eval harnesses yourself. Change how other teams build with AI.
links: Q2 Elite reviewer and GenAI fluency

goals.title: G5 Be completely reliable
goals.outcome: Zero missed commitments without prior renegotiation, tracked weekly.
goals.notes: Every commitment lands, or you renegotiate before the deadline, never after.

goals.title: G6 Move the organization and grow people
goals.outcome: One major proposal decided. Two mentees with clear progress toward Staff.
goals.notes: Change what gets funded. Make other engineers visibly better.

goals.title: G7 Stay current in design
goals.outcome: 20+ timed design katas completed, each with a written gap list.
goals.notes: Hold your own in any architecture debate, in any domain. 90 minutes each, no lookups, constraints written first.
links: Q2 Elite reviewer and GenAI fluency

projects.name: Q1 Lab and instruments
projects.goal: A lab system I can break on purpose, and the three logs that measure my judgement.
projects.description: Weeks 1-13 (2026-10-26 to 2027-01-24). Measure everything. Break things on purpose. Goals in focus: G1 systems, G3 estimation and risk, G2 reviewing.

tasks.title: Wk 1 - Create the three logs and enter the first estimate and risk call
tasks.notes: Estimates (50% and 90% range, actual), risk calls (probability, outcome), decisions. These live in /log.

tasks.title: Wk 1 - Estimate the whole Q1 lab build before starting it, and log it
Wk 2-4 - Build a small distributed system in a domain I don't know
tasks.notes: API gateway, order service with a database, queue consumer, notification service, a cache. Containers, with metrics, logs and tracing from day one. Deliverable: working system and dashboard, actual vs estimated build time.

tasks.title: Wk 5 - Break it: slow dependencies
tasks.notes: Predict with a probability what breaks, how fast, which alerts. Then inject latency; watch timeouts, thread pools, retry storms. Deliverable: prediction vs reality write-up.

tasks.title: Wk 6 - Break it: messaging
tasks.notes: Duplicate messages, out-of-order delivery, consumer crash mid-batch, rebalance. Predict first, then run, then add idempotency where it failed.

tasks.title: Wk 7 - Break it: data
tasks.notes: Cache stampede, database failover, partial writes across two services. Predict first, then run, then fix. Deliverable: failure atlas for the lab.

tasks.title: Wk 8 - Postmortem drill: five public postmortems, root cause predicted first
tasks.notes: Read only the architecture and context, write how you think it failed, then read the real root cause. Deliverable: catch-rate baseline for G2.

tasks.title: Wk 9 - Build review checklist v1 from what broke and what I missed
tasks.notes: Tier every item: blocking, important, nit. Used on every review from now on.

tasks.title: Wk 10 - Design katas 1-3: global rate limiter, double-entry ledger, real-time leaderboard
tasks.notes: 90 minutes each. Constraints first: team size, budget, deadline. Compare with a strong public reference and list the gaps.

tasks.title: Wk 11 - Estimation calibration: 15 real tasks and 5 lab tasks with 50/90 ranges
tasks.notes: Deliverable: first reference-class table.

tasks.title: Wk 12-13 - Three-person feedback ask, score the logs, finish what slipped
tasks.notes: Ask one peer, one junior and one leader: what should I do more of, and less of? Protecting slack is part of G5. Deliverable: Q1 review with three changes for Q2.

tasks.title: Wk 14-15 - Review six public design proposals cold, in four layers
tasks.notes: Kafka KIPs, Kubernetes KEPs or Rust RFCs. Read only the proposal, review, then read the real discussion: what did senior maintainers catch that you missed? Deliverable: six reviews with gap lists.

resources.name: Practice worksheets
resources.description: The three worksheets the plan runs on, kept as notes to copy per use.

notes.title: Pre-mortem worksheet
notes.body:
45 minutes with the team. 'It is six months later and this failed. Why?' Everyone writes silently for five minutes first.

For each failure story: likelihood (1-5), blast radius (1-5), detectability (1-5, where 5 is invisible), score = L x B x D, owner.

Then: top three risks and their mitigation. And the tripwire - what signal tells us a risk is happening?

Log each one in /log as a risk call with a probability and a resolve-by date.

notes.title: Design kata worksheet
notes.body:
90 minutes, no lookups. Write constraints before you draw anything.

Problem.
Constraints: team, deadline, budget.
Numbers: peak load, read/write ratio, data size.
Where contention really sits.
Top five failure modes.
What I deliberately cut.
Delivery estimate (50% / 90%) - log it in /log.

Then compare with a strong reference and score yourself 1-5 on: problem framing, correctness, failure handling, abuse and edge cases, pragmatism, judgement. Finish with: what the reference had that mine didn't.

notes.title: Decision journal entry
notes.body:
One per significant decision. Revisit at 3 and 12 months.

Date and decision.
Context: what I knew.
Options considered.
What I chose and why.
Confidence (%) - log this in /log as a risk call so it gets scored.
What would prove me wrong.

Review at 3 months: what happened?
Review at 12 months: what did I learn?
